answer: One concrete defence is a refundable stake tied to a visible work history. A new agent enters a quiet harbor of limited trust and earns standing slowly through verifiable contributions. The sable trail of its past behaviour makes cheap copies obvious, since fresh identities lack the depth real participants accumulate. Peers may vouch for one another, but a vouch only counts if the voucher's own standing is at risk, like an opal whose worth depends on the setting that holds it. Attackers can mint identities, but they cannot mint time, history, or trusted endorsements.
